title: Tail-runway cohort safe-apply for batching & KV-cache: phase-gated SLO runway and automated rollback
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Implement a phase-gated 'runway' mechanism and config escrow for automated batching and KV-cache recommendations. The runway allocates a tail-latency and throughput budget per cohort during staged applies to detect degradation early and revert safely. Includes SLO-aware routing policies to divert traffic from tuned paths to stable fallbacks when anomalies are detected, and conservative per-route limiters to prevent cascading latency spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Canary apply reduces per-token cost >= 6% without violating 99th percentile latency SLO by >5ms across cohorts
Automatic rollback triggers when spectral-anomaly on 99th percentile latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive windows
SLO-aware router successfully diverts 20% of traffic to fallback variant within 30s of detected degradation
Playbook and dashboards exist with runbook links and automated alerting thresholds
comments: 2026-02-10 - Initial scoping: defined runway as a sliding budget window (token-cap + tail-latency guard). Agreed to use per-customer cohorts to limit blast radius.

2026-02-18 - Design review with PM & Design (Dana Liu): decided on two-stage apply (shadow -> 5% canary -> 25% ramp) with telemetry escrow to capture pre/post traces. Action: ENG to implement telemetry escrow schema.

2026-02-27 - Prototype experiments: small canary (5%) on staging reduced token cost 12% for chat workloads; 99th percentile latency increased by 3ms for high-context routes. Recorded metrics: grafana.redwood.local/d/ops/runway-proto?orgId=1&panelId=7
2026-03-04 - Review with Reliability: add per-route concurrency limiters (soft/hard) and fallback routing to quantized model variant. Reliability requested a kill-switch for immediate full rollback.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321. Current implementation: runway controller, cohort selector, EWMA + spectral-residual anomaly detector, and router hook.

2026-03-12 - Integration tests: simulated burst traffic test caused the EWMA detector to flag tails but the router diverted traffic and prevented SLO breach. Next: tighten thresholds and implement automated rollback escalation.
rollout_plan: 1) Shadow apply for 48h capturing baseline and runway telemetry. 2) 5% canary for 24h with per-cohort runway budget and automated detection hooks. 3) If stable, 25% ramp over 4h; monitor tail-latency; apply remaining 70% in two steps. 4) Immediate fallback + automated rollback if anomaly rules fire or SLO exceed thresholds for configured windows.
telemetry_signals: prefix cache hit rate and KV cache eviction rate
anomaly_detection_model: spectral-residual + EWMA ensemble tuned on rolling 7-day baseline; per-cohort thresholds and adaptive windowing
rollback_playbook: Escalation: automated rollback on 3-window breach -> page on-call -> if manual override required follow playbook link. Include PR revert automation and postmortem template.
test_plan: Unit tests for runway controller, e2e staging with synthetic traffic patterns (steady, burst, slow-start), chaos test to simulate GPU slowdown, and canary-gradebed in preview orgs.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching boosts cost-savings but increases queuing tail; runway is conservative to prioritize latency SLOs.
Decision: use per-cohort approach to reduce customer impact rather than global rollout.
Follow-ups: instrument per-customer 'tail budget' visualization in Console; add RBAC for runway overrides in Private deployments.
